about.size: Large reef grouper; adults commonly reach several feet. NOAA describes fish occurring to about 200 m depth.
about.diet: Juveniles feed mainly on crustaceans, especially shrimp. Adults primarily eat fishes and squid.
about.swimming_depth: Near-bottom reef habitat from shallow water to about 200 m; adults move into progressively deeper water as they grow.
about.behavior: Generally solitary and relatively site-attached outside spawning. Adults occupy rocky bottoms, drop-off walls, ledges, caves, crevices, coral reefs and artificial reefs. Juveniles use seagrass and oyster-rubble habitat in parts of the range; Florida Keys juveniles also use reef habitat.
about.timing_note: Patterns reported by local captains and fishing writers, not tested by studies.
